name: AgencyAnalytics
tagline: White-label marketing dashboards and client reports that pull from dozens of ad, SEO and social platforms.

pricing.basis: monthly, tiers scale by number of client campaigns
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: If you report on two or three data sources for a handful of clients, an agent can absolutely build you a dashboard that pulls GA4, Search Console and Google Ads and emails a branded PDF on the first of the month. That covers most of what a small shop actually uses. What it does not cover is the long tail: the eighty-plus connectors, each with its own OAuth dance, rate limits, schema changes and silent deprecations, which is the entire product for anyone juggling Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, Shopify, call tracking and six CRMs. Keyword rank tracking is worse, because you cannot scrape SERPs reliably and a SERP API is just another subscription with another bill. So the build is real but it is a weekend, not a sitting, and it stays honest only as long as your connector list stays short.
coreLoopDIY: Pulls metrics from a few Google APIs into a local database on a schedule and renders a branded per-client dashboard plus a monthly PDF.
requirements: Google Cloud project with GA4 Data API, Search Console API and Google Ads API enabled
OAuth client credentials or a service account with access granted on each client property
Somewhere to run a nightly job (a small VPS or a laptop that is actually on)
SMTP credentials if you want reports emailed
A SERP API subscription if you want rank tracking at all
whatYouLose: Eighty-plus maintained connectors, and the person who fixes them at 2am when Meta ships a breaking change
Keyword rank tracking and the historical SERP data behind it
Client-facing login portals with per-client permissions
Report templates and white-label polish that look deliberate instead of homemade
Scheduled delivery you can trust without checking that the cron fired
moatNotes: The moat is not the charts, it is the hundred API contracts someone else renegotiates every quarter.
whyPeopleStillPay: Agencies pay because reporting is a cost center that must never be the reason a client churns. One connector breaking mid-month is a bad conversation with someone paying you five figures, and a subscription converts that risk into a line item. The breadth is also not optional once you have ten clients, because each one arrives with a different stack and nobody wants to write a TikTok Ads integration to onboard a dentist. The DIY version works great right up to the moment your client list stops looking like your data sources.
notes: The dashboard is a weekend; the connector fleet is a full time job. Keep your source list to three and this is genuinely fine.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted marketing reporting dashboard for a small agency. Stack: Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, and Recharts. No external services beyond the Google APIs below.

Data sources, in scope:
- Google Analytics 4 Data API: sessions, users, conversions, top channels, top landing pages
- Google Search Console API: clicks, impressions, CTR, average position, top queries
- Google Ads API: spend, clicks, impressions, conversions, CPA (make this one optional behind a feature flag, it is the fiddliest)

Out of scope, do not stub or fake: Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, Shopify, call tracking, keyword rank tracking, client logins.

Requirements:
- Credentials come from .env only (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, refresh tokens per client, SMTP_*). Commit a .env.example, never real values.
- A clients.json config file defines each client: display name, logo path, accent color, GA4 property ID, Search Console site URL, optional Ads customer ID.
- A single ingest script (npm run ingest) fetches the last 90 days for every client and upserts daily rows into SQLite. Idempotent, safe to re-run, logs per-source failures without aborting the whole run.
- Dashboard route /c/[client] renders the client's metrics with month-over-month deltas and the client's logo and accent color. One page, no tabs.
- npm run report -- --client=acme --month=2026-09 renders that month to PDF with Playwright and optionally emails it via SMTP.
- Store raw API responses in a blobs table so a schema change does not lose history.
- Seed the database with generated fake data so the UI is reviewable before any credentials exist.

Deliver a README that states plainly which APIs need which scopes, how to grant access per property, and the fact that adding a non-Google source means writing a new connector by hand.
